A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SiM research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original SiM experiments on vision and NLP benchmarks, including performance comparisons, computational measurements, robustness tests, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 2–6 and Tables B–H.

M1.justification: The SVD-based task subspaces, minimum-residual routing, compressed task-vector integration, and grouped inference are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same vision collections up to 50 tasks, seven NLP tasks, unseen-task scenario, and CUB-200/SUN397 fine-grained scenarios. The appendix experiments newly highlighted in v2's main text already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix experiments, including merging methods and distance-based task classifiers. The expanded discussion of RegMean, Fisher-Merging, and ReTeX does not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same models, data splits, training budgets, and evaluation procedures. The default 32 support samples and rank setting of 10% of feature dimension are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same rank, support-sampling, transformer-block, hard-versus-soft-routing, and routing-error analyses, alongside unseen-task and fine-grained tests. v2 adds pointers to these existing analyses rather than new tests.

E5.justification: Table F in both versions reports means and standard deviations across five seeds, numbered 0–4, for support sizes from 1 to 32. The repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practice are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table B retains TSV-C+SiM accuracies of 90.0 and 80.2 for 30 and 50 tasks. The oracle-routing gap emphasized in v2 was already reported in v1's Appendix E.5.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the subspace and residual definitions, and the mathematical descriptions of compressed task vectors are unchanged. No theoretical results, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free task identification, routing without known task IDs, compatibility with compressed experts, and improved merged-model performance. The new code statement does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of separability, routing errors, intermediate-layer features, and efficiency are retained, as are Appendix F's data-access limitations. New main-text summaries repeat interpretations already present in v1's appendices.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a SiM code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. The documented pseudocode, hyperparameters, expert preparation, and hardware information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds ReTeX and distinguishes its parameter-recovery use of feature-space identification from SiM's direct use in dynamic merging. It also expands explanations of already cited static and subspace-based methods, without broadly changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 expands the related-work prose, adds explicit appendix cross-references and an Appendix heading, and makes small affiliation and bibliography edits. Appendix E.4 removes an incorrect Table G(b) reference. The overall section structure and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Layout reflow changes figure placement relative to surrounding text, including Figures 3–4 appearing above Section 4.2 in v2. Title wrapping and hyperlink colors also change. The figures and table structures are retained without new or redrawn scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a code repository pointer, clearer related-work context, and direct links from the main narrative to existing appendix evidence. Removing the incorrect Table G(b) callout also improves navigation. These are modest gains in clarity and reproducibility documentation; the method and empirical support remain unchanged.
